briefing.headline: OpenAI Orion-2 and xAI Colossus-3 push AGI benchmarks into new territory as compute arms race intensifies.

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: Frontier labs released multiple high-capability models this week, with OpenAI and xAI leading in multimodal reasoning. Global regulatory pressure mounts while investment remains robust at $11.9B quarterly. Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production systems.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI deployed Orion-2 achieving 87% on ARC-AGI, while Anthropic's Claude 4.5 and Google's Gemini 3.0 advanced agentic capabilities. Meta open-sourced Llama 4 405B and DeepSeek released R2 with strong coding performance. xAI Colossus-3 demonstrated unprecedented scale in training.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: New research highlights persistent prompt injection risks across LLM APIs. DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level for multi-agent, automotive, and BCI systems.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: NVIDIA shipped 1.2M H200 GPUs this quarter as Microsoft and Google expand data center footprints in Texas and Arizona. TSMC reports record AI chip demand with 3nm yields improving.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will regulatory fragmentation slow US labs enough for Chinese frontier models to close the capability gap by 2028?
